parsed.rationale: Deploying mfa:admin and mfa:dbadmin together blocks exfiltration, and no single control is enough. Exfiltration needs admin on db, fileserver or backup. Each of those needs a foothold from auth_db, auth_fileserver or auth_backup, which require stolen_dbadmin AND (NOT mfa_dbadmin OR admin_dc OR admin_adfs). With mfa_dbadmin deployed, the attacker would need admin_dc or admin_adfs. Those require a foothold on dc or adfs, which needs NOT mfa_admin, so mfa_admin closes that route and all three auth steps are blocked. No single control works. With only mfa_admin: the attacker phishes for a workstation foothold and stolen_user, pivots internally, authenticates to ciserver (the workstation foothold bypasses mfa_user), kerberoasts for stolen_admin, escalates ciserver, leaks stolen_dbadmin, then authenticates to db and exfiltrates. With only mfa_dbadmin: the same path yields stolen_admin, then auth_dc and escalate_dc give admin_dc, which bypasses mfa_dbadmin. With only segmented: phishing plus escalate_workstation gives admin_workstation, which satisfies the pivot condition. Any single patch leaves these credential-based paths open, since phishing is always available. Note that segmented + patched:workstation + patched:laptop also works (3 controls) by blocking reach_internal, but it is not minimal.
